reference.title: An enhanced color visual cryptography scheme based on the binary dragonfly algorithm

requirements.reference_requirement: Separate R, G and B matrices with original spatial dimensions
Generate an intensity histogram separately for R, G and B
XR, XG, XB are 8-bit color-level variables (24 bits total)
Select color levels that minimize PSNR + correlation coefficient between original and share images
BDA operations applied to all three channels during the same optimization process
requirements.source_note: Section 4.3; supplied MATLAB BDA has XR/XG/XB together

requirements.reference_requirement: 1000 BDA iterations used to identify optimal color levels
For channel X, divide its histogram into NX regions containing approximately equal numbers of pixels
If r<P/2 both share pixels are 0; otherwise both are 255
Assign (0,255) or (255,0) according to the paper probability split
Combine R/G/B binary channel shares into two RGB shares
Shares have the same dimensions as the original image
Use V3 transfer |DeltaX/sqrt(1+DeltaX^2)| and probabilistic bit flipping

ambiguities.detail: The paper states fitness(PSNR + CC) from original-vs-share comparisons, but does not uniquely specify whether Share 1, Share 2, their sum, mean, minimum, or another aggregation is used.
ambiguities.impact: Current Python implementation uses the mean across Share 1 and Share 2.

ambiguities.detail: The paper says minimize CC and later says ideal CC is zero. Direct minimization of signed Pearson CC could reward strongly negative correlations, which conflicts with the stated zero-correlation security goal.

ambiguities.issue: NX range includes invalid group counts
ambiguities.detail: The paper describes XR/XG/XB as 8-bit values ranging 0-255, but share generation uses P=k/(NX-1); NX=0 or NX=1 is mathematically invalid as a number of histogram groups.
ambiguities.impact: Current executable implementation clamps decoded NX to [2,255].

ambiguities.detail: The paper treats low PSNR as desirable encryption quality for original-vs-share comparison, but nearby prose also discusses recovered-image quality. Its reported PSNR and MSE values are not mutually consistent under the standard 8-bit PSNR formula.
ambiguities.impact: Do not interpret low original-vs-share PSNR as reconstructed-image PSNR. Keep secrecy and reconstruction metrics separate in the new study.

ambiguities.detail: The paper requires equal numbers of pixels per group, but identical intensity values cannot always be split into strictly equal histogram regions without splitting an intensity bin.
ambiguities.impact: Current implementation uses deterministic cumulative-histogram quantile boundaries; group populations are therefore approximately equal when ties occur.
